findings.reason: the plan should fold a named entry into the existing rank/position contract (or state the composition and mutual exclusion) rather than add a parallel selector whose interaction with `source_rank` is undefined.
findings.text: §4 gives a binding an optional slot naming one entry of the first struct array by its `name` leaf so one binding family and one structure assembly per coil can read the ragged pf_active store, but `_read_ids_path`/`_struct_array_positions` already drive struct-array traversal from `binding.source_rank` (`preserved_positions` stacks the trailing structural arrays or collapses to `[0]`), so the plan introduces a second, overlapping traversal mode inside one function and states only "a binding without it reads exactly as today" — it does not say how the selector composes with `source_rank`/`preserved`, nor why entry selection cannot be expressed through the rank/position mechanism that already decides which struct-array entries are read

findings.reason: the plan should justify why the selection cannot ride the existing `StructureAssembly` identity (or extend it) before adding a binding-level duplicate of the same fact.
findings.text: the new binding slot repeats a fact the catalogue already declares: `StructureAssembly.member_bindings` names the binding families of a conductor and `StructureAssembly.element_identifiers` names its emitted elements, and `geometry_adapter._assembly_identifiers` (imas_ambix/data/geometry_adapter.py:256) already resolves a family to its assembly and identifiers; adding the source-entry name on the binding makes the binding a second place a struct-array entry's identity is written, so MAST's per-coil pattern is duplicated rather than expressed through the owner

deep_module-1.reason: Acted in plan v89: section 4 states the selector consumes the first struct level and source_rank counts the levels below it.

duplicate_owner-1.reason: The selector is the binding's source address, the job MAST's per-coil source_array does; StructureAssembly keeps naming emitted elements after the transform. Plan v89 states this in section 4.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §4's newest repair adds a binding-level struct-array selector that overlaps, rather than folds into, the traversal contract already owned by `_read_ids_path`/`_struct_array_positions`.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4's new binding slot makes the binding a second owner of struct-array-entry identity, which the catalogue already owns in `StructureAssembly.member_bindings`/`element_identifiers`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — `public_definitions` 0, `cli_options` 0, `mcp_views` 0, `refusal_families` 0; each section that adds interface surface accounts for it in its own text — §2's "one public function ... retires nothing, because ambix has no exporter"; §4's store slots "retire nothing, because the catalogue had no addressing slot" and "the probe-angle key retires the machine branch"; §4's selector "widens one binding contract and retires nothing, because no binding could select a struct-array entry before"; §5 "adds one data file and no public definition or refusal family"; §7 "adds two record fields and retires nothing" and "the label is widened in `resolve_shotset_version` rather than a second labeller added". No section adds to a family without the required statement.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and reuses the owning mechanism for nearly every addition it proposes: §6 supplies an observation cohort to `imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py` `score_convention`/`format_sign_report` and a loader to `imas_ambix/challenge/convention.py` `_integrated_current` rather than writing a second scorer; §6/§7 share `imas_ambix/gs/operator.py` `build_operator`/`vacuum_prediction` as the one forward operator; §7 extends `imas_ambix/eval/efit_referee.py` `judge_geometry` through the existing `read_efit_geometry(..., loader=...)` seam and reads geometry through `gs/artifact_resolution.py`/`spine_bench/machine_artifact_arm.py` rather than a second resolver; §4 extends `NetCDFTransformEngine` rather than adding a deck engine; §7 reuses `SshTransport`. Every one of these is checked against the code and holds.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan's layers extend existing machinery with justification rather than wrapping it: §4 widens `StoreEngine.open` (already landed as `machine_map`/`store_layout` parameters, verified in `imas_ambix/data/transform_engine.py:155,267`) because "no engine has a way to see the map today"; §7 adds the EQDB reader "beside the §3 extractor's and reuses its ssh transport ... rather than a second path"; §2 keeps the exporter out of the loaders.
